I have checked t1 routes and was surprised that routes for t1 are statically configured on VMs. I thought that we use dynamically announced routes for all topologies.

comments.author: wangxin
comments.body:
@msosyak. I checked from my side. Egress ACL testing will fail on platforms that do not support egress ACL. Please check whether the platform you are using supports egress ACL.

Could you try limiting ACL test cases to "TestBasicAcl and ingress" to see if the results look better?

The result from my side is `1 failed, 45 passed, 322 deselected`.  The only failed case is `TestBasicAcl.test_source_ip_match_forwarded[ingress-tor->spine]`.  I suspect it was because the ACL configuration is not set down to ASIC yet since this case is the third one been executed. The two previous test cases are to verify that packets should be dropped:
* acl/test_acl.py::TestBasicAcl::test_unmatched_blocked[ingress-tor->spine]
* acl/test_acl.py::TestBasicAcl::test_unmatched_blocked[ingress-spine->tor]
They can pass anyway even if ACL configuration is not ready yet.

I can see two issues with the test_acl.py script from the observation:
1. Need to wait some time to run test cases after the ACL rules are loaded.
2. Need to adjust the test case execution sequence. For example, promote case `test_source_ip_match_forwarded` in front of `test_unmatched_blocked`

comments.author: msosyak
comments.body: @wangxin I use the following expression to limit acl tests `-k acl and not egress and not reboot and not port_toggle` and all failed tests have ingress direction. Will play with a timeout after rule applies, but for me is strange that the same tests that fail on `t1` pass on `t1-lag`(same hardware/no changes).

@wangxin 
The t0 and t1-lag routes have been changed after replacing static routes on VM with exabgp announced routes, But t1 not. So the DST_IP_TOR = '192.168.0.1' is point to the spine. This caused the acl testing failed on all spine->tor direction on t1 topology.

Summary:
Fixes #1785 

The VM startup config template for t1 topology is still using static
route. Update the templates to use exabgp announced routes like t1-lag
topologies.

### Type of change

<!--
- Fill x for your type of change.
- e.g.
- [x] Bug fix
-->

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] Test case(new/improvement)

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
The VM startup config template is still using static IP routes for t1 topology. This caused the ACL testing failed on t1 topology.

#### How did you do it?
* Update the t1 startup config templates to symbolic links to t1-lag startup config templates.
The t1-lag config templates will skip configuration of PortChannels if the topology file does not have PortChannel information. It can be re-used for t1 topology which does not have PortChannels.
* Update the t1 topology file to remove un-used variables.
* Update the PTF backplane IP address in the t1 topology file.

#### How did you verify/test it?
* Deploy a t1 topology.
* Run test_announce_routes.
* Run the test_acl.py script.
